## TASK-004 - Implement safe project and profile loading

Create the ontology skill package and its standard-library loader with explicit project root, strict JSON parsing, identity checks, confined local contexts and ontology-specific binding allowlists.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `planned` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-016, REQ-048 |

| Target artifacts | SKILLS-depo/ontology/SKILL.md, SKILLS-depo/ontology/scripts/ontology.py, SKILLS-depo/ontology/scripts/ontology_core.py, SKILLS-depo/ontology/tests/test_loading.py |
| Dependencies | None |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- Preserve unrelated bytes and stop on stale inputs or a scope conflict.

### Acceptance criteria

- Wrong/missing/neutral identities, duplicate JSON keys, traversal, symlinks, forbidden source paths, remote contexts and unsupported profile features fail with bounded diagnostics.
- Loading opens only selected modules and bindings; same-label projects remain isolated and no network or package setup occurs.

### Planned verification

- Run source test_loading tests under .venv/bin/python with bytecode writes disabled.
- Use disposable same-label projects, escaping/symlink references and a network-disabled fixture; compare filesystem inventories before/after loads.

### Risks

- Preserve unrelated bytes and stop on stale inputs or a scope conflict.

### Acceptance criteria

- Identical source/config/module/helper inputs produce byte-identical projections with no clock or temporary absolute path noise.
- Invalid input cannot publish a success manifest; an explicit rebuild restores deleted generated projections without changing canonical or durable records.
- Only declared generated destinations are written; unrecognized user-owned files are preserved and conflicts reported.

### Planned verification

- Compile twice and compare every output byte; remove generated fixture output and explicitly rebuild it.
- Inject validation and write failures and confirm unchanged canonical, durable and unrelated file hashes.
